items.title: Erdogan vows to keep Turkey out of Iran war's 'ring of fire'

featured_image.name: President Recep Tayyip Erdogan is throttling Turkey's democracy

items.description:
Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan on Tuesday vowed that Turkey would remain outside the widening conflict engulfing the Middle East, delivering a pointed rebuke of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and warning that the world's eight billion people are paying the price for what he called "Netanyahu's war for survival."

Speaking after a cabinet meeting in Ankara on the 25th day of the US-Israeli air campaign against Iran, Erdogan said Turkey is "determined to keep our country out of this ring of fire" and rejected attempts by warring parties to draw Ankara into the conflict.[1][2]

"We are not falling into traps set for us," Erdogan said, according to Turkey's state-run Anadolu Agency. "The past 25 days have shown that while this is Israel's war, the world is paying the price."[2]

items.title: Iran stops all gas exports to Turkey after South Pars strike

featured_image.name: Iraq suffers major power capacity loss as Iran halts gas flows after South  Pars strike | The National

items.description:
Iran has stopped all natural gas exports to Turkey following Israel's March 18 strike on the South Pars gas field, Bloomberg News reported on Tuesday, citing people familiar with the matter. The halt marks the latest energy disruption from an attack that has sent shockwaves through global markets and intensified a broader confrontation across the Middle East.[1][2]

Turkey purchased approximately 14% of its natural gas from Iran last year, according to data from the Turkish Natural Gas Distributors Association cited by Bloomberg. According to Türkiye Today, roughly 75% of Iranian gas flows to Turkey had already been cut in the immediate aftermath of the strike before the full halt took effect. The Turkish Energy Ministry declined to comment on the situation.[2][3][1]

items.title: Iran fires cluster bomb missile at Bnei Brak, injuring 9

featured_image.name: Building collapses after Iranian missile strike on Israel

items.description:
Nine people, including six children, were injured on Tuesday after an Iranian ballistic missile carrying a cluster bomb warhead struck the central Israeli city of Bnei Brak, dispersing bomblets over a wide area that also reached nearby Petah Tikva. The attack was one of several Iranian missile barrages that struck Israeli cities throughout the day as the conflict between Iran and a U.S.-Israeli coalition entered its fourth week.

Magen David Adom, Israel's emergency medical service, reported that a 23-year-old man was in moderate condition with shrapnel wounds, while eight others — including six children — sustained mild injuries from blast effects and shrapnel. Footage from the scene showed cluster submunitions scattered across residential areas, a weapon type Iran has repeatedly deployed against Israeli population centers during the war.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Israel says it killed Quds Force operative in Beirut strike

items.description: The Israeli military and Shin Bet announced on Tuesday that they killed Muhammad Ali Kourani, described as a member of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Quds Force, in a naval strike on the Beirut area carried out the previous day. The Israeli Defense Forces said Kourani had been "advancing terror attacks directed by Iranian intelligence officials" from within Lebanon.[1][2]

items.title: Second projectile hits Iran's Bushehr nuclear plant in a week

featured_image.name: Iran's Bushehr nuclear plant hit by projectile, no damage reported; IAEA  calls for caution

items.description:
A projectile struck the perimeter of Iran's Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant on Tuesday evening local time, the Atomic Energy Organization of Iran reported, marking the second such incident at the facility in just over a week. The strike, which occurred at approximately 9:08 p.m. local time on March 24, resulted in no casualties, damage, or disruption to operations, according to Iran's state news agency IRNA.[1][2]

The IAEA confirmed it had been informed by Iran of the latest projectile impact at the plant. Iran's atomic energy organization accused the United States and Israel of carrying out the attack.[3][4][5]

items.title: CENTCOM says 9,000 targets hit in Iran campaign's first 24 days

featured_image.name: CENTCOM: 9,000 Iranian targets hit so far

items.description: US Central Command announced on March 23 that Operation Epic Fury has struck more than 9,000 military targets inside Iran since the campaign began on February 28, marking one of the largest American military operations in the Middle East in decades. The updated fact sheet, published by the Department of Defense, also confirmed more than 9,000 combat flights and the destruction or damage of over 140 Iranian naval vessels across the first 24 days of the operation.[1][2][3]

items.title: US sends Iran 15-point plan to end Middle East war

featured_image.name: US proposes new nuclear deal to Iran during 4th round of talks

items.description: The United States has transmitted a 15-point plan to Iran aimed at ending the war in the Middle East, now in its fourth week, according to The New York Times, citing two officials briefed on the diplomacy. The proposal, delivered through Pakistan, outlines sweeping demands on Iran's nuclear and ballistic missile programs alongside provisions for the Strait of Hormuz, though it remains unclear whether Tehran views it as a viable basis for negotiations.[1]

items.title: Hezbollah's missile stockpile down to one-sixth of pre-war levels, Israel says
items.description:
Israel's military estimates that Hezbollah now possesses between 11,000 and 13,000 missiles and rockets, a sharp reduction to roughly one-sixth of the arsenal the Iranian-backed group held before October 2023, according to The Wall Street Journal. CNN separately confirmed the figures, reporting that the group's stockpile has been depleted after years of sustained Israeli strikes.[1][2][3]

The assessment, provided by an Israeli military representative, represents a dramatic decline from the approximately 75,000 missiles and rockets Hezbollah was believed to possess before the Hamas-led attack on Israel in October 2023, according to estimates by the Alma Research and Education Center, an Israeli security think tank.[4][1]

items.title: Israel renews Beirut bombardment, killing 3 including child

featured_image.name: Beirut under fire as Israel expands air strikes in Lebanon

items.description:
An Israeli airstrike on a residential apartment in the town of Bchamoun, about 10 kilometers southeast of central Beirut, killed at least three people including a three-year-old girl early Tuesday, Lebanon's Health Ministry said. Five others were wounded in the predawn attack, which came as Israel renewed its bombardment of the Lebanese capital after a two-day lull.[1][2]

Online footage showed flames engulfing at least one apartment in the struck building. The attack on Bchamoun, located in the Aley district of Mount Lebanon, hit outside the southern suburbs of Beirut where Israel had previously ordered evacuations and concentrated its strikes against Hezbollah.[2][1]
